title: Reservoir-conditioned virtual returns generate random Liouvillian skin localization in a reciprocal Mott insulator
authors: Y. T. Wang, X. Z. Zhang, W. M. Liu
abstract: Directional dissipation can concentrate relaxation modes in space, but connecting this accumulation to controlled microscopic processes in correlated matter requires separating virtual charge motion from spin coherence. We study this connection in a half-filled Hubbard chain with reciprocal hopping and number-conserving, direction-selective returns of virtual doublon--hole defects. Eliminating charge defects and then Mott coherences yields asymmetric spin-exchange rates under an explicit separation of timescales, with full short-chain dynamics supporting the reduction on finite exchange times. Balanced random returns concentrate the stationary population and several low-lying right modes at sample-selected positions rather than a predetermined edge, producing random Liouvillian skin localization despite zero end-to-end logarithmic rate bias. The accumulated rate imbalance determines an exact finite-density hard-core stationary state and a one-particle activated relaxation scale governed by random barriers. This connection between locally calibrated return rates, many-body stationary weights and slow relaxation offers a means of controlling transport in constrained open quantum matter without changing the reciprocal Hamiltonian.
summary: This work investigates how directional dissipation in a Mott insulator can be controlled by separating virtual charge motion from spin coherence. By analyzing the dynamics through a two-stage reduction, the authors show that random return processes induce random Liouvillian skin localization. This establishes a novel link between local return rates and the macroscopic control of quantum transport in constrained open systems.
main_problem: The paper aims to connect directional dissipation arising from virtual charge motion to controlled microscopic spin-exchange processes in correlated matter.
main_result: Reservoir-conditioned virtual returns generate asymmetric Mott exchange, leading to random Liouvillian skin localization even when the end-to-end bias vanishes.
method: The study employs a two-stage reduction process on the Hubbard-Lindblad dynamics, separating charge defect elimination from Mott coherence suppression to derive effective population rate equations.
model_or_system: The system is a half-filled Hubbard chain with reciprocal hopping, analyzed using a full Hubbard-Lindblad dynamics approach, which is then reduced via timescale separation.
key_observables: Random Liouvillian skin localization, asymmetric spin-exchange rates, finite-density hard-core stationary state, and one-particle activated relaxation scale.
important_parameters: The analysis relies on a strict hierarchy of timescales ($t/\sqrt{D_0} \ll 1$, $\gamma_m/\kappa_0 \ll 1$, etc.) for the reduction to be valid.
main_assumptions: The derivation requires an explicit separation of timescales and assumes that the final rate ratios are robust even if source lifetimes are unequal.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how balanced random returns cause sample-selected accumulation (random localization) compared to fixed-edge accumulation under uniform bias.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the full Hubbard-Lindblad dynamics, applying a two-stage reduction (charge elimination then coherence suppression), deriving the effective rate equations, and finally analyzing the resulting localization properties and stationary states.
why_interesting: It provides a detailed theoretical framework for controlling transport in open quantum systems by engineering local return rates, which is highly relevant for understanding dissipation in quantum materials.
